meta.title: Adv. Grammar Test (C1-C2) - Avengers Universe
meta.description: A comprehensive test covering advanced English grammar topics themed around the Avengers universe, combining at least two or more advanced concepts per question.
meta.info: This test includes 30 questions focusing on combined C1-C2 level grammar structures such as inversion with conditionals, subjunctive with cleft sentences, and more, featuring characters like Dr. Strange, Hulk, Iron Man, and others.
meta.author: Qwen3.7

explanation.text: This combines negative adverbial inversion ('Hardly had... looked') with a mixed conditional. The 'if' clause refers to a past unreal condition (past perfect 'had consulted'), and the main clause refers to a past unreal result ('would have been').
explanation.concept: Negative inversion with past unreal conditions
explanation.formula: Hardly + had + subject + past participle ... would have + past participle + if + subject + had + past participle
examples: Hardly had he looked when he realized it would have been better if he had consulted her.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the mandative subjunctive ('it is imperative that it be') with a cleft sentence. The relative pronoun 'who' refers to the singular 'investigator', so the verb must be 'signs'.
explanation.concept: Mandative subjunctive in it-clefts
explanation.formula: It is imperative that + subject + base verb + who/that + singular verb
examples: It is essential that it be the manager who approves the budget.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This sentence combines a perfect passive participle clause ('Having been exposed') with an advanced passive reporting structure ('is believed to have transformed').
explanation.concept: Perfect passive participles and passive reporting verbs
explanation.formula: Having been + past participle, subject + is believed + to have + past participle
examples: Having been warned about the risks, the project is believed to have failed.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: By 2026, Steve will have been frozen for over a century, so he _____ significant culture shock.

explanation.text: This combines the future perfect continuous ('will have been frozen') with a modal verb of deduction about the past/present ('must have experienced'), indicating a strong logical conclusion based on duration.
explanation.topic: Future Perfect Continuous + Modal Verbs of Deduction
explanation.concept: Duration up to a future point leading to past/present deduction
explanation.formula: Subject + will have been + verb-ing + for + time, so + subject + must have + past participle
examples: He will have been working there for years, so he must have learned the system.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines a reduced relative clause (past participle 'trained' for passive meaning) with a gerund pattern after 'regret' ('having betrayed' for a past action).
explanation.topic: Reduced Relative Clauses + Gerunds vs. Infinitives
explanation.concept: Past participle reduction and gerund after regret
explanation.formula: Noun + past participle + verb + having + past participle
examples: The documents signed yesterday regret having contained errors.

data.hint: Choose the correct words to complete the elliptical sentence with a discourse marker.
data.question: Although _____ devastating, Asgard was, _____, rebuilt.

explanation.text: This combines ellipsis in an adverbial clause of concession ('Although seemingly' omits 'it was') with a formal discourse marker of contrast ('nevertheless').
explanation.concept: Omission in adverbial clauses and contrast markers
explanation.formula: Although + (subject + be) + adjective, clause, nevertheless, clause
examples: Although (it was) difficult, the mission was, nevertheless, successful.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines a noun clause acting as the subject ('What makes...') requiring a singular verb ('is'), with a double comparative structure ('the more... the more...'). 'It' takes the singular verb 'holds' and 'becomes'.
explanation.concept: Subject-verb agreement in noun clauses and double comparatives
explanation.formula: What + singular verb + is + that + the + comparative + subject + singular verb, the + comparative + subject + singular verb
examples: What is important is that the harder you try, the better you get.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: Scott is accustomed to _____ down, despite his friends warning him against _____ with the quantum realm.

explanation.text: This combines verb patterns requiring a gerund after a preposition ('accustomed to' + gerund, 'warning against' + gerund) with separable phrasal verbs ('shrink down', 'mess with').
explanation.concept: Preposition + gerund and phrasal verb usage
explanation.formula: Subject + be + accustomed to + gerund + despite + noun + warning against + gerund
examples: I am used to working late, despite them warning me against staying up.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines adjective + preposition collocations ('oblivious to', 'susceptible to') with article usage. 'Unique' starts with a consonant sound (/j/), so it takes 'a', not 'an'.
explanation.concept: Adjective collocations and indefinite articles before consonant sounds
explanation.formula: Adjective + to + noun phrase + a + word starting with /j/ sound
examples: She was oblivious to the fact that it was a unique chance, leaving her susceptible to errors.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to ensure subject-verb agreement.
data.question: Neither of the proposed strategies _____ effective, although a number of alternatives _____ under consideration by Fury.

explanation.text: This combines quantifiers with subject-verb agreement rules. 'Neither of' takes a singular verb ('has proven'), while 'a number of' means 'several' and takes a plural verb ('remain').
explanation.concept: Singular vs. plural verbs with specific quantifiers
explanation.formula: Neither of + plural noun + singular verb; A number of + plural noun + plural verb
examples: Neither of the options is viable, but a number of ideas are being discussed.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines 'If only' for past regret (requiring past perfect 'had acted') with 'It's high time' for present urgency (requiring past simple 'stopped').
explanation.topic: Wish / If Only + It's High Time
explanation.concept: Past regret and present urgency structures
explanation.formula: If only + subject + past perfect; It is high time + subject + past simple
examples: If only I had known; it is high time we left.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: Wanda behaves as though she _____ the sole ruler of Westview, and so chaotic _____ her magic that reality bends.

explanation.text: This combines an unreal comparison using 'as though' (requiring past subjunctive 'were') with 'so + adjective' inversion ('so chaotic is her magic').
explanation.topic: As Though / As If + So / Such Inversion
explanation.concept: Unreal comparisons and emphatic inversion
explanation.formula: Subject + verb + as though + subject + past subjunctive, and so + adjective + be + subject
examples: She acts as though she knew everything, and so confident is she that no one argues.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines third conditional inversion ('Had Carol Danvers not absorbed') with 'not only... but also' inversion ('not only would she... but the Kree would also...').
explanation.topic: Conditional Inversion + Not Only ... But Also
explanation.concept: Inversion in conditionals and correlative conjunctions
explanation.formula: Had + subject + past participle, not only + auxiliary + subject + verb, but + subject + would also + verb
examples: Had I known, not only would I have helped, but they would also have stayed.

data.hint: Choose the correct inverted structures to complete the sentence.
data.question: Little _____ that under no circumstances _____ the Skrulls reveal their true form voluntarily.

C.text: did Fury know / the Skrulls would

explanation.text: This combines two negative adverbial inversions. 'Little' at the beginning of a clause requires 'did Fury know', and 'under no circumstances' requires the auxiliary 'would' to precede the subject 'the Skrulls'.
explanation.topic: Little Did He Know + Under No Circumstances
explanation.concept: Double negative adverbial inversion
explanation.formula: Little + auxiliary + subject + verb + that + under no circumstances + auxiliary + subject + verb
examples: Little did they know that under no circumstances would he agree.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines first conditional inversion ('Should you need') with second conditional inversion ('were I to build'). Both require the base form of the verb, and the main clause requires 'would' for hypothetical results.
explanation.topic: Should You Need + Were I To
explanation.concept: Conditional inversion for future possibility and hypothetical situations
explanation.formula: Should + subject + base verb, were + subject + to + base verb, subject + would + base verb
examples: Should you require help, were I to assist, I would be glad.

data.hint: Choose the correct structures to complete the sentence.
data.question: _____ the manuscript, containing Hydra's secrets, that _____ Bucky's memories.

explanation.text: This combines an it-cleft sentence ('It was the manuscript... that triggered') with a present participle clause acting as a reduced relative clause ('containing Hydra's secrets').
explanation.concept: Emphasis using it-clefts and present participle reduction
explanation.formula: It + was + noun + , + present participle + , + that + past tense verb
examples: It was the letter, containing the truth, that changed everything.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines a mixed conditional (past condition, present result) with the mandative subjunctive. After 'demanded that', the verb must be in the base form ('be'), and the main clause uses 'would be struggling' for an ongoing present result.
explanation.concept: Past unreal condition with present result and mandative subjunctive
explanation.formula: If + subject + had + past participle + that + subject + base verb, subject + would + be + verb-ing
examples: If he had demanded that she be present, we would not be struggling now.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the relative clause.
data.question: The hammer, which _____ to have been enchanted by Odin, can only be lifted by the worthy.

explanation.text: This combines a non-defining relative clause ('which is said') with an advanced passive reporting structure ('to have been enchanted').
explanation.concept: Passive reporting verbs in non-defining relative clauses
explanation.formula: Noun, which + is/are + said/thought/believed + to have been + past participle, + main verb
examples: The ruins, which are believed to have been built by Romans, were found.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines modal verbs of deduction about the past ('must have', 'can't have') with gerund patterns. 'Regret' and 'enjoy' are both followed by a gerund ('adopting', 'enjoyed isolating') when referring to the action itself.
explanation.topic: Modal Verbs of Deduction + Gerunds vs. Infinitives
explanation.concept: Past deduction and verb patterns requiring gerunds
explanation.formula: Subject + must/can't + have + verb + gerund
examples: He must have regretted quitting, as he can't have enjoyed being unemployed.

data.hint: Choose the correct structure to complete the comparative sentence.
data.question: The more resources Thanos gathered, _____ for the Avengers to stop him.

explanation.text: This combines the double comparative structure ('the more... the harder...') with standard word order (no inversion in the second clause).
explanation.concept: Double comparatives with standard word order
explanation.formula: The + comparative + subject + verb, the + comparative + subject + verb
examples: The sooner we start, the earlier we will finish.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines a discourse marker ('however' for contrast) with noun clauses. The subject clause 'what we need' is singular, so it requires the singular verb 'is', not 'are'.
explanation.concept: Subject-verb agreement in noun clauses with discourse markers
explanation.formula: Whatever + clause, discourse marker, it is evident that + what + subject + base verb + is + singular noun
examples: Whoever they are, however, it is clear that what matters is the result.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: Rocket is accustomed to _____ with adversaries who are prone to _____ him.

explanation.text: This combines verb patterns where 'to' functions as a preposition ('accustomed to' + gerund) with an adjective + preposition collocation ('prone to' + gerund).
explanation.concept: Preposition + gerund patterns
explanation.formula: Subject + be + accustomed to + gerund + who + be + prone to + gerund
examples: He is used to working late, and he is prone to making mistakes when tired.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines quantifiers ('few of' for countable, 'little of' for uncountable) with a phrasal verb ('survived the blast'). 'Soil' is uncountable, so it requires the singular verb 'was'.
explanation.concept: Countable/uncountable quantifiers and phrasal verb usage
explanation.formula: Few of + plural countable noun + past tense verb, and little of + uncountable noun + singular verb
examples: Little of the advice was useful, and few of the suggestions lived up to expectations.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: I wish the entirety of the Avengers _____ present, but the number of casualties _____ to rise.

explanation.text: This combines 'wish' + past subjunctive for present unreal situations ('were' for the collective plural 'Avengers') with subject-verb agreement rules ('the number of' takes a singular verb 'continues').
explanation.concept: Past subjunctive after wish and singular verbs with 'the number of'
explanation.formula: I wish + plural subject + were, but the number of + plural noun + singular verb
examples: I wish the students were quieter, but the number of disruptions continues.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines 'It's high time' + past simple ('stopped') for present urgency with 'as though' + past subjunctive ('knew') for an unreal comparison.
explanation.topic: It's High Time + As Though / As If
explanation.concept: Past simple for present urgency and past subjunctive for unreal comparisons
explanation.formula: It is high time + subject + past simple + as though + subject + past simple
examples: It is high time he stopped behaving as though he owned the place.

data.hint: Choose the correct words to complete the inverted sentence.
data.question: _____ devastating was the snap that _____ the Avengers not found a way back, humanity would have perished.

explanation.text: This combines 'so + adjective' inversion ('So devastating was') with third conditional inversion ('had the Avengers not found'). 'Such' is used with nouns, while 'so' is used with adjectives.
explanation.concept: Emphatic inversion and conditional inversion
explanation.formula: So + adjective + be + subject + that + had + subject + not + past participle, subject + would have + past participle
examples: So dangerous was the path that had we not been careful, we would have fallen.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines 'not only' inversion ('Not only did Tony create') with 'little' inversion ('little did the public know'). Both negative adverbials at the start of a clause require subject-auxiliary inversion.
explanation.topic: Not Only ... But Also + Little Did He Know
explanation.concept: Double negative adverbial inversion
explanation.formula: Not only + auxiliary + subject + verb, but + little + auxiliary + subject + base verb
examples: Not only did she win, but little did anyone know she was injured.

data.hint: Choose the correct inverted structures to complete the sentence.
data.question: Under no circumstances _____ activate the helicarrier, _____ you value the safety of the crew.

explanation.text: This combines negative adverbial inversion ('Under no circumstances should you') with first conditional inversion ('should you value'). Both require the auxiliary verb to precede the subject.
explanation.topic: Under No Circumstances + Should You Need
explanation.concept: Negative inversion and conditional inversion
explanation.formula: Under no circumstances + auxiliary + subject + base verb, should + subject + base verb
examples: Under no circumstances should you open this, should you value your safety.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines second conditional inversion ('Were I to open') with an it-cleft sentence ('it would be the Mirror Dimension that I would choose'). 'Were I to' must be followed by the base verb.
explanation.concept: Conditional inversion and emphasis using it-clefts
explanation.formula: Were + subject + to + base verb, it would be + noun + that + subject + would + base verb
examples: Were I to decide, it would be this path that I would take.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the mixed conditional passive sentence.
data.question: If the super-soldier serum _____ not _____, Steve would not be considered a living legend today.

explanation.text: This combines a mixed conditional (third conditional 'if' clause for a past unreal condition + second conditional main clause for a present unreal result) with advanced passive structures ('had not been administered', 'would be considered').
explanation.concept: Past unreal condition with present result in passive voice
explanation.formula: If + subject + had + not + been + past participle, subject + would + be + past participle
examples: If the letter had not been lost, we would be informed by now.
